description: Hi! I’m Mohammad Abbas, a CS student skilled in Python, FastAPI, Next.js, AI/ML integration, and cybersecurity. I specialize in rapid, API-first prototyping to ship working MVPs fast. Join my team for reliable backend/AI execution as we build Astro FIT, an astronaut health monitoring platform. Looking for a UI/UX designer, frontend dev (React/Figma), and a strong presenter/pitcher passionate about space-tech or health analytics. Let’s team up and build something impactful!
summary:
Astro FIT is an autonomous astronaut health monitoring and clinical decision-support telemetry system designed for long-duration space missions. Built around NASA Human Research Program (HRP) guidelines for the five hazards of human spaceflight: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity fields, and hostile closed environments. The platform empowers astronauts to independently evaluate and manage their physical and behavioral health.

The software features an interactive anatomical body map with color-coded system diagnostics, dynamic multi-day telemetry charts, multi-modal vital logging (including a cognitive reaction-time test and diagnostic image upload), and a mission scenario simulator across orbital, transit, lunar, and rover environments. Because deep-space missions face communication delays of up to 20 minutes with Earth, real-time flight surgeon consultation is impossible. Astro FIT bridges this critical autonomy gap by translating raw biomarkers into plain-language risk assessments, step-by-step self-exam instructions, and actionable NASA-aligned countermeasures protecting crew safety and mission readiness beyond low-Earth orbit.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Astro FIT is an autonomous astronaut health monitoring and clinical decision-support platform designed for long-duration space missions. Grounded in NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP) research on the 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight (Space Radiation, Isolation & Confinement, Distance from Earth, Gravity Fields, and Hostile Closed Environments), the system gathers multi-modal health indicators and translates complex biomedical data into clear, actionable medical guidance.

  • Interactive Anatomical Diagnostic Map: A clickable clinical schematic of the human body highlights four critical physiological systems—Neuro-Behavioral, Cardiovascular, Musculoskeletal, and Radiation/Immune—using ISO-standard semantic color coding (Nominal, Caution, Critical) for immediate situational awareness.
  • Multi-Modal Data Logging & Cognitive Testing: Astronauts can manually log vitals (blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep duration, and radiation dose), upload diagnostic ultrasound/ocular scans for visual assessment, and complete a built-in 15-second Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT) reaction test to objectively measure cognitive fatigue.
  • Autonomous Countermeasure & Self-Exam Engine: Clicking any body region or receiving an alert reveals plain-language risk explanations, step-by-step instructions on how to perform self-exams in microgravity, and automated NASA-aligned treatment protocols (such as ARED resistive exercise adjustments, hydration/electrolyte intake, circadian light therapy, or storm-shelter relocation during solar particle events).
  • Multi-Environment Mission Simulator & Gamified Readiness: Users can switch across four mission environments (ISS Orbital Station, Mars Deep-Space Transit, Lunar Surface Base, and Pressurized Rover) and simulate emergency scenarios, while a gamified daily health checklist and Crew Readiness Score encourage consistent preventative care.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact

As humanity prepares for lunar bases and crewed missions to Mars, communication delays with Earth can reach up to 20 minutes one-way—making real-time consultations with ground flight surgeons impossible during acute medical events. Astro FIT bridges this autonomy gap by acting as an onboard clinical co-pilot. It reduces cognitive overload during high-stress emergencies, empowers non-physician crew members to perform accurate self-assessments, and promotes proactive preventative care so small physiological dips do not escalate into mission-critical medical emergencies. Beyond spaceflight, this offline-first, self-guided diagnostic architecture can also support remote terrestrial environments such as polar research stations, submarines, and underserved rural clinics.

Tools, Technologies & Software Used

  • Frontend & UI Architecture: React, TypeScript, Next.js, and Tailwind CSS styled with an authentic, high-contrast flight-deck telemetry aesthetic (flat matte surfaces, tabular monospace readouts, and zero-clutter visual hierarchy).
  • Data Visualization & Interactivity: Recharts and custom responsive SVG schematics for dynamic multi-day biomarker trendlines, threshold bands, and interactive anatomical hot-spots.
  • Clinical Rules & Simulation Engine: Custom TypeScript/Python rule-based evaluation engine mapped to NASA HRP risk thresholds and countermeasure protocols, supported by an AI Flight Surgeon assistant powered by Google Gemini / AI Studio.
  • Development & Deployment: Built and prototyped using Google AI Studio, VS Code, Git/GitHub, and Vercel.

Creativity & Key Design Considerations

  • Designed for Autonomy & Stress: Rather than overwhelming astronauts with raw medical jargon or flashy "sci-fi" visuals, we engineered an authentic aerospace console interface focused on rapid glanceability, plain-English explanations, and step-by-step self-exam guidance—assuming an astronaut may need to diagnose themselves while fatigued or under stress.
  • Behavioral Engagement: Recognizing that compliance drops on multi-month missions, we integrated gamified mission streaks and a live Mission Readiness Percentage so routine health checks feel rewarding rather than tedious.
  • Environment-Aware Baselines: Our team specifically accounted for how physiological baselines and hazard priorities shift depending on whether a crew member is in microgravity transit, conducting a physically demanding lunar EVA, or confined inside a pressurized rover.
